description: YONPA — embeddable, triggered, per-project codebase-maintenance system. YON workflows ('automators') composed into 'clusters' on @younndai/yon-runner, persisted in a per-project libSQL substrate. The two YONPA-specific records below (@AUTOMATOR, @CLUSTER) are runtime-expanded by YONPA; pure-spec parser-validation is shape-only.

records.description: YONPA automator — typed identity + registry fields for a YON workflow that yon-runner executes under YONPA's HIL discipline. Runtime-expanded by YONPA into @AGENT + adjacent @META records; pure-spec parser-validation covers shape only. See yai.yonpa metadata.use_cases for expansion semantics.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Automator identifier — kebab-case, conventionally y-prefixed

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable display name

fields.name: mission
fields.description: One-line statement of what this automator does
fields.example: Reduce verbosity within a single file

fields.name: layer
fields.description: YONPA library layer

fields.name: tier
fields.description: Execution tier — what the automator needs to run. Distinct from `protection_tier` (impact friction).

fields.name: version
fields.description: Automator semver (independent of YONPA's own version)

fields.name: yonpa_schema_version
fields.description: Which yai.yonpa schema version this automator is authored against. YONPA's convention linter refuses authoring against fields not present in the bundled schema at this version. Addresses silent partial-propagation drift across the automator chain.

fields.name: protection_tier
fields.description: Impact-friction tier. Distinct from execution `tier`. Default `normal` if omitted. High-tier edits require a hybrid cooling-off period on top of standard HIL gates.

fields.name: delegates_to
fields.description: Harness-skill reference this automator wraps (e.g. a Claude Code or Codex skill name). Nullable; many automators are native YONPA workflows with no delegation.

fields.name: confidence_threshold
fields.description: Per-automator confidence floor. Below this threshold the automator auto-escalates via @ESCALATE rather than auto-applying. Defaults per harm-class if omitted: read-only=0.6, mutators=0.75, high-impact mutators=0.85, verification=0.9, overseers=0.7.

fields.name: hil_gates
fields.description: Declarative list of @STEP rids that require HIL approval (comma-separated). Documentation in v1 (YONPA convention linter validates the rids resolve); future runtime injection of @ESCALATE is a v2 capability. If tier=mixed|reasoning, the linter expects at least one entry.

fields.name: consumes_directives
fields.description: Which directive levels this automator consults at run time (comma-separated subset of L0,L1,L2,L3). Default: all four.

fields.name: install_scope
fields.description: Registry scope: `global` (user-level, all projects) or `local` (this repo only). Local overrides global by id.

records.description: YONPA cluster — composed workflow expanded at run time into a coordinated set of automator invocations. A pre-existing sugar tag, now formalized as a yai.yonpa record. The `phases` field is encoded as a string because the schema format doesn't support nested object arrays — YONPA's convention linter validates the phases structure (see metadata.use_cases for the workaround).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Cluster identifier — kebab-case

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable display name; defaults to capitalized id

fields.name: yonpa_schema_version
fields.description: Schema-version pin (same purpose as on @AUTOMATOR). Linter-enforced.

fields.name: members
fields.description: Member automator ids (comma-separated). YONPA convention linter validates each id resolves in the automator registry.

fields.name: phases
fields.description: Phase definitions as a YON-encoded structure. Pure-spec parser-validation only checks that the field is present as a string. YONPA's convention linter parses and validates the nested structure (n:int, agents:[...], mode:enum, scope, role, gate:bool, etc.) per Appendix A of YON-MAPPING.md. The nested-object limitation in schema-format.md is tracked as a yon-spec RFC candidate.

fields.name: success
fields.description: Free-text success criterion expression; evaluated by yPrime at cluster completion
fields.example: patches verified + no directive violations + report archived

fields.name: install_scope
fields.description: Same semantics as on @AUTOMATOR.

meta.tagline: Per-project codebase-maintenance system built on YON workflows

use_cases.title: Schema precedes product — preview status
use_cases.description: yai.yonpa is registered BEFORE YONPA itself ships. As of 2026-05-24 YONPA is design-locked but the build has not started; @younndai/yonpa is not yet npm-published. This domain is a forward-looking schema authority claim, not a description of shipping behavior. Authors discovering @AUTOMATOR/@CLUSTER through the domain registry should treat them as 'preview — runtime expansion requires the YONPA runtime, which is not yet released.'
steps: Note: parser validates shape only; no public runtime exists yet to expand the records
Wait for YONPA v1 publication (gated on @younndai/yon-runner publication AND a YONPA v1 build per PT-4) before authoring against this schema for production use
use_cases.example: @AUTOMATOR id=example | name="Example" | mission="shape preview" | layer=refactor | tier=reasoning | version="0.1.0" | yonpa_schema_version="1.0"

use_cases.title: Runtime expansion requirement — pure-spec validation is shape-only
use_cases.description: Both @AUTOMATOR and @CLUSTER are runtime-expanded by YONPA. A pure-spec yon-parser (with @younndai/domains loaded) validates field shape — required fields, enum values, patterns, types — but does NOT execute the expansion. The records remain in unexpanded form unless YONPA's runtime processes them. Consumer parsers that report a YONPA file as 'valid' are reporting shape-validity, not operational completeness. Do not infer behavior from validation alone.
steps: Parser validates @AUTOMATOR/@CLUSTER field shape (free, via bundled domains)
YONPA convention linter validates cross-record rules (hil_gates rids resolve to @STEP rids; phases nested structure parses)
YONPA runtime expands @AUTOMATOR → @AGENT + adjacent @META; @CLUSTER → full @WORKFLOW (per YON-MAPPING.md Appendix A; ≈15× expansion for clusters)
Without YONPA's runtime, the records are valid YON but operationally inert

use_cases.title: yonpa_schema_version pin — silent-drift prevention
use_cases.description: Every @AUTOMATOR and @CLUSTER record MUST carry a `yonpa_schema_version` field. The YONPA convention linter enforces that the value is ≤ the bundled yai.yonpa schema version. This catches a silent partial-propagation failure mode: a yai.yonpa schema bump propagated to some links in the chain but not others would otherwise let unknown fields preserve silently under YON forward-compat — bypassing security-sensitive fields like `protection_tier=high`. Parser-level refusal of mismatched-version unknowns would require a yon-spec RFC against the forward-compat preservation rule; tracked separately as a future enhancement. The linter-primary path covers this case without a spec change.
steps: Author's bundled yai.yonpa is at 1.1 — convention linter refuses (author needs to upgrade their YONPA install)
Author's bundled yai.yonpa is at 1.2+ — linter accepts; fields validated normally

AUTOMATOR.purpose: Typed identity + registry fields for a YONPA automator. Replaces the prior @AGENT + adjacent @META convention for YONPA automator authoring.
AUTOMATOR.when_to_use: Authoring a YONPA automator .yon file. Materialize directly into a yon-runner workflow via YONPA's runtime expander.

CLUSTER.purpose: Composed workflow shorthand expanded at run time into a coordinated set of automator invocations. The original YONPA sugar tag, now formalized as a domain record.
CLUSTER.when_to_use: Authoring a YONPA cluster file as shorthand for several automators that should run together under one coordination pattern.

related.reason: YONPA acts on codebases; some automators wrap build / lint / test operations via the yonpa:shell plugin
YONPA has memory but no soul (no cognition loop, no autonomy). A hard design line keeps it strictly distinct from SAI, which is the system that does have those.
